---
title: "The standards landscape"
description: "Which standards apply to your analysis, what each is for, and when it bites."
---

Several standards govern analysis in government. They overlap, they are not all mandatory for all
work, and it is not obvious from their titles which apply to you.

This section says what each is for and, more usefully, **when it bites**.

## The short answer

::: {.callout-note title="Which applies to your work" appearance="minimal" icon=false}
<br>
**All NHSBSA analysis** follows GovS 010 and the AQuA Book.

**Official statistics** additionally follow the Code of Practice for Statistics. That is a narrower
set of outputs than "everything we publish".

**Analysis involving code** additionally follows the NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook.

**Appraisal and evaluation** additionally follow the Green and Magenta Books.
:::

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-standards.qmd >}}

Getting the boundary wrong is costly in both directions. Applying the full Code of Practice to a
routine internal data request wastes effort the organisation does not have. Failing to apply it to
an official statistic is a regulatory matter.

## The two that apply to everything

### GovS 010: Analysis

The government functional standard for analysis. It sets out five principles, the governance and
accountabilities that must exist, the analytical cycle in five stages, and **thirteen supporting
practices**, which is where most of its detail sits.

The thirteen are: public interest; inputs and methods; supporting decision-making; uncertainty;
analytical verification and validation; documentation and record keeping; quality assurance;
collaborative working; learning from experience; analytical models; statistics; appraisal and
evaluation; and personal data.[^src-govs-010-sections-6-2-to-6-14] Every one of them has a section of
this playbook that answers to it, and
[appendix A2](../A-appendices/index.qmd) says which.

**What is binding.** The standard separates *shall*, a requirement, from *should*, a recommendation.
*Shall* appears eleven times, once in the conventions table that defines it, and seven of the
remaining ten require a different functional standard to be followed. Only three are substantive
requirements, and they are set out in [section 1](../01-why-quality-matters/index.qmd). Everything else, the thirteen practices included,
is a *should*: a departure you have to be able to explain rather than an option you may take or
leave.

**When it bites:** always. It applies to all analysis undertaken in government, whoever does it.

NHSBSA is assessed against GovS 010, and improving that assessment is why this playbook exists.

### The AQuA Book

Guidance on producing quality analysis for government. Where GovS 010 sets the requirement, the
AQuA Book says how to meet it.

It is the source of the analytical lifecycle in [section 4](../04-analytical-lifecycle/index.qmd),
which is its four stages[^src-aqua-book-section-5-2]; of the proportionality approach in
[section 5](../05-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd), which is its chapter 3[^src-aqua-book-chapter-3]; of the four roles in [section 3](../03-roles-and-responsibilities/index.qmd)[^src-aqua-book-section-5-1]; and of the **RIGOUR** principles.[^src-aqua-book-section-1-3-5]

### RIGOUR, in full

**Repeatable.** For an analytical process to be considered "valid" it might reasonably be expected
that for the "same" inputs and constraints the analysis produces the "same" outputs. Different
analysts will consider the analytical problem differently, potentially resulting in differing
results; but if any one approach is repeated the results should be as expected. Repeatable is not
the same as automated, and
[section 6](../06-doing-the-work/index.qmd) sets out the difference.

**Independent.** To produce analysis that is free of prejudice or bias. In doing so, care should be
taken to appropriately balance the views across all stakeholders and experts.

**Grounded in reality.** Quality analysis takes the commissioner and analyst on a journey as views
and perceptions are challenged and connections are made between the analysis and its real
consequences. Connecting with reality in this way guards against failing to properly grasp the
context of the problem being analysed.

**Objective.** Effective engagement and suitable challenge reduces potential bias and enables the
commissioner and the analyst to be clear about the interpretation of the analytical results.

**Uncertainty-managed.** [Uncertainties](../07-uncertainty/index.qmd) have been identified, managed
and communicated throughout the analytical process.

**Robust.** Provide the analytical result in the context of residual uncertainty and limitations in
order to ensure it is used appropriately.

It is also the more prescriptive of the two documents, and by some margin. Read it as the stricter
of the pair wherever they overlap.

**When it bites:** always, as the practical companion to GovS 010.

## The one that applies to official statistics

### The Code of Practice for Statistics

Maintained by the UK Statistics Authority and regulated by the Office for Statistics Regulation.
Edition 3.0 has been in force since 30 October 2025.

It keeps the three pillars of **Trustworthiness, Quality and Value**, and sets out ten Standards for
Official Statistics beneath them.

| Standard | Pillar | Producers must |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Show integrity | Trustworthiness | Act honestly, objectively and professionally, and challenge misuse |
| 2. Lead responsibly | Trustworthiness | Make impartial decisions under the Head of Profession for Statistics |
| 3. Be transparent | Trustworthiness | Release at a standard time, pre-announced |
| 4. Manage data responsibly | Trustworthiness | Handle data safely and be open about its use |
| 5. Prioritise quality | Quality | Support a quality culture that encourages learning and improvement |
| 6. Be rigorous | Quality | Use suitable data and sound methods, and assure quality across production and release |
| 7. Be open about quality | Quality | Explain strengths, limitations and uncertainty prominently |
| 8. Be relevant | Value | Put users at the centre of decisions about the statistics |
| 9. Be clear | Value | Present statistics to support appropriate interpretation |
| 10. Be accessible | Value | Ensure statistics are accessible and freely available to all |

**When it bites:** for official statistics, in full and as a regulatory requirement. NHSBSA official
statistics are listed in the
[statistical collections](https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/statistical-collections).

::: {.callout-note title="You may apply the Code voluntarily" appearance="minimal" icon=false}
<br>
Those producing data, statistics or analysis that is **not** official statistics may still apply the
Code to demonstrate a commitment to trustworthiness, quality and public value.[^src-govs-010-section-6-12]

That is worth considering for anything published or quoted externally. It is a choice, not an
obligation, and choosing it should be a deliberate decision rather than an accident.
:::

**Standards 5, 6 and 7 are what most of this playbook is about.** Following
[section 5](../05-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) and
[section 6](../06-doing-the-work/index.qmd) is how NHSBSA meets them in practice.

## The ones that apply to particular work

| Standard | What it covers | When it bites |
|---|---|---|
| **NHSBSA Analytical Code Assurance Playbook** | Version control, testing, peer review, readable and modular code, documentation, open sourcing | Whenever your analysis involves code |
| **NHSBSA Data Science Playbook** | The workflow for Data Science initiatives: problem definition, assigning a critical friend, analysis, wrap up | Data Science initiatives |
| **NHSBSA Open Data Standards** | How NHSBSA publishes open data | Open data releases |
| **Green Book** | Appraisal of policies, programmes and projects: costs, benefits and risks of alternatives | Appraisal work |
| **Magenta Book** | Evaluation: assessing an intervention's design, implementation and outcomes | Evaluation work |
| **Orange Book** | Risk management principles and concepts | Assessing analytical risk. Referenced by GovS 010 section 4.2 |
| **Government Data Quality Framework** | Managing and describing data quality | Where data quality is a material concern |
| **Data and AI Ethics Framework** | Using data and AI appropriately and responsibly. Seven principles | See [section 10](../10-ethics-and-transparency/index.qmd) |
| **Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard** | Publishing how an algorithmic tool informs decisions | Where an algorithmic tool informs a decision affecting the public |
| **AI Playbook for the UK Government** | Ten principles for building, buying and using AI in government | Where your analysis builds on or uses an AI system |
| **Introduction to AI assurance** (DSIT) | Assurance mechanisms for AI systems: risk assessment, algorithmic impact assessment, bias audit, compliance audit, conformity assessment, formal verification | Where an AI system has to be evaluated rather than just built |

### If your analysis uses AI or an algorithmic tool

This playbook covers analysis. It does not cover building or assuring AI systems, and you should not
read it as though it does. What it can tell you is which obligations attach.

- **The Data and AI Ethics Framework applies, in full.** Its scope was extended to AI and algorithmic
  technologies in December 2025 and its seven principles cover both. [Section 10](../10-ethics-and-transparency/index.qmd)
- **The Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard may apply.** If an algorithmic tool informs a
  decision affecting the public, a record is expected. NHSBSA already has published records, so there
  are worked examples to follow. The analyst drafts the record as part of delivery and the Head of
  Profession for Statistics owns submission, because an ATRS record is a public statement about a
  tool and needs the same sign-off as a published statistic.
- **The AI Playbook's ten principles apply to the system**, and DSIT's assurance mechanisms are how
  it gets evaluated. Both are linked in [section 12](../12-tools-and-templates/index.qmd).
- **An AI system can still be Business Critical**, and if it is, [section 8](../08-business-critical/index.qmd)
  applies on top of everything above.

**The short version is that AI analysis is assured the same way as any other analysis**, plus the
transparency duties named above. This playbook signposts the AI estate rather than duplicating it,
because building and assuring an AI system is a different subject with its own guidance, and a
playbook that half-covers it would be worse than one that points at the guidance that covers it
properly.

## How they fit together

They are layers rather than alternatives, and they rarely conflict.

GovS 010 sets the requirement. The AQuA Book explains how to meet it. The Code of Practice adds
obligations for official statistics. The code assurance playbook adds obligations where there is
code. The Green, Magenta and Orange Books add depth for particular kinds of work. The AI estate applies
on top when a system rather than an analysis is what is being assured.

**Where two sources appear to conflict, the more specific and more recent governs, and you should
raise it.** If this playbook disagrees with a standard, the standard is right and this playbook needs
fixing. Say so via the route in [section 13](../13-getting-help/index.qmd).

## The five NHSBSA playbooks

This is one of five, and they are designed to work together rather than overlap.

| Playbook | Use it for |
|---|---|
| **Producing Quality Analysis**, this one | Planning, assuring and communicating any piece of analysis |
| [Analytical Code Assurance](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-analytical-code-assurance-playbook) | Version control, testing, peer review and documentation of analytical code |
| [Data Science](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-data-science-playbook) | The end-to-end workflow for a Data Science initiative |
| [Data Visualisation Standards](https://nhsbsa.github.io/nhsbsa-digital-playbook/data/data-visualisation/) | Charts, tables and dashboards, in the Digital, Data and Technology Playbook |
| Official Statistics | Developing, maintaining and publishing official statistics. In development |

If your work involves code, you need this playbook and the code assurance one. If it is a Data
Science initiative, the Data Science Playbook is the one that sequences your work. If it produces a
chart, a table or a dashboard, the Data Visualisation Standards say how it should look and how it
should be labelled.
